Solids-free liquid and gas products from the filter pass through a heat exchanger containing a water-cooled coil (Fig. S3), then through a back-pressure regulator (BPR) into the product collection vessel. At the cooler outlet, a thermocouple is used to monitor flow temperature and prevent hot fluids (>70 °C) from entering the BPR and damaging the diaphragm. Nitrogen gas from a pressurized cylinder and an air-driven gas booster provides pressure to the dome-side of the BPR diaphragm. After cooling and depressurization, liquid and gaseous HTL products enter an ambient-pressure metal drum (69 L) where the gaseous products vaporize. The drum’s vent is equipped with an activated carbon air filter (details in Table S1) to manage odors (which proved to be a major consideration as the distinct and unpleasant smell of “cooked algae” can be detected in other rooms (nearby offices) in the building).

Instrumentation on the CFR included six thermocouples: between the preheater and the PFR, within the lower, middle, and upper zones of the PFR, within the filter vessels, and between the cooler and the BPR. The thermocouples in the preheater/PFR were connected with micro-controllers and solid-state relays for programming of the band heaters. In addition to the differential pressure gauges on the filter vessels, seven regular pressure gauges were used on the CFR: at the outlet of the metering pump, at the outlet of the PFR, on each of the two filter vessels, on each of the two blow-down pots, and at the inlet of the cooler.

steps.title: Assemble feed supply system
steps.instruction: Install the 114 L cylindrical feed tank equipped with a C‑clamp mounted agitator, connect the 841 µm pore‑size cylinder filter (with a pass‑by valve for cleaning), and attach the high‑pressure metering pump capable of 0–250 mL/min flow and up to 34.5 MPa pressure; set the pulsation dampener to approximately 80 % of the system pressure and install a pressure transducer for continuous pressure monitoring.

steps.title: Install reaction heating system
steps.instruction: Connect the feed line to the preheater set to a mild 133 °C to avoid premature liquefaction, power the 4.5 kW preheater to achieve an instant heating rate of 150 °C min⁻¹ using a short‑tube coil, then install the vertical plug‑flow reactor (PFR) and attach three ceramic band heaters (4 kW lower, 2 kW middle, 2 kW upper) with fiberglass insulation as specified in Table S1.

steps.title: Install dual high‑pressure filter system
steps.instruction: Mount two parallel high‑pressure cylinder filter vessels (each 1.9 L volume, 10 µm pore size, 405 cm² filter area) upstream of the cooler; ensure the HTL product enters the filters at ~220 °C and ~17.3 MPa, set the product flow through the filters to 130–180 mL/min, connect a diaphragm differential‑pressure gauge and set the cleaning trigger at 0.34 MPa, and attach blow‑down pots (7.9 mm I.D. connector, water‑jacketed, with a relief valve and a 25 µm screen for solid collection).

steps.title: Connect pressure let‑down and cooling
steps.instruction: Route the solids‑free liquid and gas from the filter outlets through a water‑cooled coil heat exchanger, place a thermocouple at the cooler outlet to keep the temperature ≤70 °C before the back‑pressure regulator (BPR), supply nitrogen gas and an air‑driven booster to the dome side of the BPR diaphragm, and collect the cooled product in a 69 L ambient‑pressure metal drum equipped with an activated‑carbon vent filter.

steps.title: Install safety and auxiliary components
steps.instruction: Between the pressure transducer and the preheater install check valves and 31.4 MPa @ 350 °C rupture discs; add an auto‑relief valve (20 MPa) and a manual relief valve after the PFR, a second 31.4 MPa @ 350 °C rupture disc downstream of the PFR, and 19.2 MPa @ 350 °C rupture discs on each filter‑vessel lid; plumb all rupture‑disc outlets with gentle curves to a stainless‑steel safety tank.

steps.title: Wire instrumentation and pressure gauges
steps.instruction: Install six thermocouples (preheater‑PFR junction, lower/middle/upper PFR zones, each filter vessel, cooler‑BPR junction) and connect them to micro‑controllers and solid‑state relays for band‑heater programming; install differential‑pressure gauges on the filter vessels and seven pressure gauges at the metering‑pump outlet, PFR outlet, each filter vessel, each blow‑down pot, and the cooler inlet.

steps.title: Perform initial system cleaning
steps.instruction: Pump 8 L of 12.5 wt % alkaline degreaser (KYZEN) through the entire CFR loop, then rinse with clean water at 300–350 °C and 10–17.3 MPa; after rinsing lower the temperature to 125 °C, rapidly release BPR pressure to generate turbulence and loosen dead‑zone sediments; combust stainless‑steel filter elements in a muffle furnace at 545 °C for 6 h, soak them overnight in 2.7 L of 1 M nitric acid, and clean the PTFE BPR diaphragm with soap and water.

steps.title: Commission reactor with water
steps.instruction: Run water through the assembled system, gradually increasing temperature and pressure to the target operating conditions (e.g., 300 °C, ~10 MPa), verifying thermocouple readings and pressure profiles at each stage before proceeding to HTL runs.

steps.title: Measure residence time distribution (RTD)
steps.instruction: Establish steady water flow at the desired temperature (25 °C or 350 °C) and pressure, inject 1.5 L of phenol tracer solution (60 mg L⁻¹) into the feed tank, collect effluent samples after the BPR, measure phenol concentration with a Lambda 35 UV‑Vis spectrometer, and calculate RTD parameters (E(t), t_m, σ², Pe) using equations (1)–(5) provided in the manuscript.

steps.title: Run hydrothermal liquefaction of algae slurry
steps.instruction: Feed 31 L of algae slurry (solids loading 3 wt % or 5 wt %) into the system, set reactor temperature to 325–350 °C, maintain flow rates of 152–155 mL min⁻¹ (giving theoretical residence times of 3–9 min), monitor temperature and pressure throughout, collect liquid product in 25 mL aliquots every 10–20 min and store at 4 °C, and collect solid residues from the blow‑down pots, freeze‑dry them and store in a desiccator; calculate carbon yield using Eq. (6) and N/C ratio using Eq. (7).

steps.title: Perform in‑situ filter cleaning during operation
steps.instruction: When the differential‑pressure gauge reaches 0.34 MPa, close the solids‑outlet and purge‑gas inlet valves of the active filter, divert HTL flow to the alternate filter, manually open the solids‑outlet valve to the ambient‑pressure blow‑down pot, allow the pressure‑difference “scrape” to discharge solids through the 7.9 mm I.D. connector into the water‑jacketed pot, vent and cool the pot, transfer solids through the 25 µm screen to a storage drum, close the solids outlet, repressurize the emptied filter vessel with compressed nitrogen via the gas booster, gradually reopen valves to avoid violent water evaporation, and allow the filter to refill with fresh HTL product (≈20–30 min, during which the main CFR outflow pauses).

steps.title: Conduct routine post‑run maintenance
steps.instruction: After each HTL run repeat the alkaline‑degreaser cleaning and water rinse as in step 7, inspect and, if needed, replace any ruptured discs, verify integrity of check valves and rupture discs, and perform a visual inspection of tubing for deposits.

steps.title: Adjust parameters for high solids loading
steps.instruction: For slurries ≥4.2 wt % solids set the preheater temperature ≤142 °C, maintain a minimum flow rate of ≥147 mL min⁻¹, back‑flush the pre‑pump cylinder filter at least every 25–30 min, and keep the filter inlet flow at 130–180 mL min⁻¹; if operating at >4 wt % solids, avoid flow rates <147 mL min⁻¹ to prevent particle settling.
